title: What is disliked (makruh) in Salah
intro: Things a Muslim should avoid in Salah – they disturb a calm and dignified prayer.

learn.html: Makruh things are acts that are disliked for a Muslim and should be avoided. In Salah, makruh means leaving out a sunnah without meaning to, or doing something that is not part of Salah and disturbs a calm, dignified prayer.

items: turning, adjusting clothes or something else during Salah
kneeling or sitting improperly without need
answering a salam with the hand, a gesture or a nod
making the second rak‘ah longer than the first
reciting the same surah in both rak‘ahs of a fard (unless you know only one)
reciting in the second rak‘ah a surah that comes before the one in the first (e.g. Al-Masad after Al-Ikhlas)
skipping just one surah between two rak‘ahs (e.g. Al-Ikhlas, then An-Nas)
going into ruku‘ or sajdah before the imam and coming back with him
praying when food is served and you are hungry
praying in a row when there is a gap in the row in front
praying in clothes with pictures of living beings, or in a room with such pictures
praying facing an open flame or on a busy path
praying on someone else’s land without the owner’s permission
praying in the open without putting a sutrah (a stick about 80 cm high) in front

learn.html: Some of these stop being makruh if the prayer time is running out, or if we might miss the jama‘ah – for example, if the time is about to end, we pray even in a room with pictures rather than lose the prayer.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: If we do something makruh, we do not have to repeat the Salah – but we should avoid it and take care to do the sunnah acts.

practice.title: Makruh or fine?
practice.prompt: Tap everything that is makruh in Salah, then tap Check.

options.text: 👕 Fixing your clothes again and again
🍽️ Praying while hungry food is on the table
📍 Looking at the place of sajdah
options.why: That is what we should do in Salah.

options.text: 🧍 Standing calmly in a straight row
options.why: That is good – it is part of praying properly.

options: Something disliked that we should avoid

questions.q: Must we repeat Salah if we do something makruh?
options: No – but we should avoid it

questions.q: In rak‘ah 1 you recite Al-Ikhlas. Which is makruh in rak‘ah 2?

options: A stick about 80 cm high put in front of someone praying

practice.title: Choose your task
prompts: 🌾 On a trip you stop in a field to pray Dhuhr; its time is nearly over and you don’t know the owner. Praying on land without permission is makruh – but the prayer time is ending. What do you do?
🤔 Someone prayed Dhuhr and forgot Al-Fatiha before the surah. They remembered only after the last sitting, right after the sajdah, and gave the salam. What should they do?
